The cardiac silhouette is normal in size and shape, indicating no cardiomegaly. The mediastinum is midline, and the hilar regions show no lymphadenopathy or masses. Both costophrenic angles are sharp and clear, which effectively rules out a pleural effusion. A noteworthy finding in the patient's radiograph is the presence of two high-density, circular metallic objects located in the lower lung regions bilaterally. These are characteristic of nipple piercings and are located externally on the chest wall. It is clinically significant to identify these as artifacts to ensure they are not misinterpreted as intrapulmonary nodules or lesions.

The second image, retrieved from a database as the most similar comparison, also demonstrates clear lungs and a normal heart size. Interestingly, it also shows a metallic piercing on the right side, highlighting that such external artifacts are common in clinical practice and can be used as a reference for identifying similar non-pathological findings. Providing this context is essential for accurate radiological interpretation and avoids unnecessary follow-up for benign external findings.
